packageRules.description: argo-events on its own, outside the weekend batch. v1.9.11 carries 4 CRITICAL CVEs in vendored Go dependencies (stdlib, grpc, pgx x2) with no fixed release available as of 2026-09-11 — scanning the 31 Aug `latest` rebuild confirmed it fixes none of them and adds one. The fix can only come from upstream, so the release should surface the day it ships rather than waiting up to a week. Placed AFTER the ArgoCD ecosystem rule so it overrides the grouping, and BEFORE the major-update rule so major bumps are still held for review. vulnerabilityAlerts does not cover this: it keys off GitHub advisories for the chart, which will not fire for CVEs vendored inside the container image.

localstack/localstack is in ignoreDeps for a hard reason, not out of neglect: 4.14.0 is the LAST release that runs without a licence. From 2026.03.0 LocalStack merged the Community and Pro images into one, and without LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN the container exits 55 at startup. Bumping it to 2026.10.4 on 2026-10-29 took the service down and had to be rolled back. The pin therefore carries 24 CRITICAL / 179 HIGH unpatchable CVEs, which is a known accepted risk on a LAN-only dev emulator, NOT something a Renovate PR can fix. Escaping it means getting a free Hobby auth token or replacing LocalStack altogether.
Automerge patch updates for non-critical tools

Application specs in manifests/applications/ are not deployed by Argo CD self-management (see CLAUDE.md). Without this note, a merged chart bump shows Synced while the cluster still runs the old chart, as happened with #1123-#1132 on 2026-11-11.
prBodyNotes:
**After merging, apply the Application spec by hand.** Argo CD does not deploy `manifests/applications/` itself:

```bash
kubectl diff -f manifests/applications/<app>.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/applications/<app>.yaml
```

Then confirm the app is Synced and Healthy **at the new chart version**. "Synced" alone can mean the old version.

packageRules.description: Calico: patch releases only. A minor bump is a CNI upgrade tied to the Kubernetes version (3.33 is planned as Phase 1 of runbooks/k8s-1.37-upgrade.md), so it is done deliberately, not proposed on a weekend. Patches still roll calico-node on every node; review before merging

flink-demo stays on Flink 2.2: the Flink Kubernetes Operator (1.16.1) accepts flinkVersion up to v2_2, and the Dockerfile pins PyFlink and the Kafka connector (5.0.0-2.2) to 2.2. PR #784 once moved the base image a major version on its own, which would have built a broken image had anyone rebuilt it. A new minor needs the operator to support it and all four to move together, by hand. After merging a 2.2.x patch, rebuild with the flink-demo-build workflow and bump the image tag

The JDK copied into flink-demo stays on Java 17: Flink 2.2 supports Java 11, 17 and 21, and the base image is a -java17 build. Renovate proposed Temurin 25 (PR #1248). Patch and update releases of 17 still come through; check the new tag has an arm64 image before merging, because the in-cluster build runs on arm64 (17.0.21.1 had none on 2026-11-21, PR #1246)

The argo-events JetStream version map (configs.jetstream.versions) is keyed by `version`, and the EventBus selects an entry by that key. Renovate bumps the image strings without the key, so on 2026-11-15 it proposed nats:2.15.3 under the entry named 2.10.29 and rewrote the 2.10.10 rollback entry (#1159-#1163). Upgrade NATS deliberately instead: add a new version entry, then point eventbus.yaml at it
Hold major updates for manual review

The generic image manager also extracts these under their pull-through registry.k8s.n37.ca names, which Renovate cannot look up (it queries our private Zot, not upstream) and which produced 'no-result' dashboard warnings. Disable those names; the dedicated customManagers extract the same images under their real upstream names instead.
